questions.scenario: It is 3 April 1933, and you are piloting one of two open-cockpit biplanes above the roof of the world. Below, Everest's summit is wreathed in blowing snow, and violent turbulent air threatens to slam your aircraft into the ridge.
questions.prompt: What do you decide as you approach the summit in dangerous turbulence?
questions.butterflyEffect: The pilots pushed through and flew directly over the summit, becoming the first men to fly over Mount Everest. Their aerial photographs gave mountaineers valuable new views of approach routes, feeding into later Everest expeditions and the broader push toward high-altitude aviation.

choices.text: Push through the turbulence and fly directly over the summit to secure photographs
Abort the mission and turn back toward the airfield at Purnea
Climb to a much higher altitude before crossing the peak
Circle at a safe distance without ever crossing over the mountain

questions.scenario: It is 3 April 2008, and you are a Texas Ranger arriving at the Yearning For Zion Ranch after a phone call from a girl claiming to be trapped in an abusive plural marriage inside the compound.
questions.prompt: What does law enforcement do upon entering the FLDS ranch?
questions.butterflyEffect: Authorities removed more than 400 children into state custody, the largest child-welfare seizure in U.S. history at the time. Courts later ruled the removal exceeded legal authority for most children, who were returned, but evidence gathered inside the ranch helped convict church leader Warren Jeffs of sexually assaulting minors in 2011.

choices.text: Remove all children on the property into state protective custody pending investigation
Arrest Warren Jeffs immediately on the scene
Permanently shut down and evict all residents from the ranch
Wait until the anonymous caller is identified before taking any action

questions.scenario: It is 3 April 2007 on the LGV Est line, and you are part of the SNCF engineering team aboard TGV V150, a specially built trainset assembled for a world speed record attempt on conventional rails.
questions.prompt: What configuration lets the train push past 570 km/h?
questions.butterflyEffect: TGV V150 reached 574.8 km/h using oversized wheels, two mismatched high-power power cars, and boosted catenary voltage. The record demonstrated the limits of wheeled high-speed rail technology and bolstered France's reputation as a high-speed rail exporter, though the modified train never entered commercial service.

choices.text: Fit larger-diameter wheels, use two extra-powerful power cars, and raise the catenary voltage
Strip out all passenger seating to reduce weight alone
Raise the catenary voltage without altering the wheels or power cars
Add jet-assisted boosters beneath the carriages

questions.prompt: How do you keep pace with the demanding cross-country schedule?
questions.butterflyEffect: Riders relayed the mail through a chain of stations, cutting the coast-to-coast delivery time to about ten days and proving a fast overland route was possible. The service folded after roughly eighteen months once the transcontinental telegraph, completed in October 1861, made it obsolete.

choices.text: Hand off the mail to a fresh horse and rider every ten to fifteen miles
Ride the entire route yourself without any relief
Wait for stagecoach connections at each town along the way
Delay departure until telegraph confirmation of the route ahead

questions.butterflyEffect: Tunisian security forces stormed the museum and killed both gunmen, Yassine Labidi and Saber Khachnaoui, ending the siege. questions.butterflyEffect: Vuia's aircraft rolled forward on its own wheels and briefly lifted about 11 meters into the air, proving a wheeled, self-propelled takeoff was possible without rails or catapults. questions.butterflyEffect: On 27 September 1986, the band's tour bus overturned near Ljungby, Sweden, killing bassist Cliff Burton. Jason Newsted joined within weeks, and the album went on to be regarded as a landmark of thrash metal despite the shadow cast over its tour.

choices.text: Cliff Burton died when the tour bus overturned in Sweden
James Hetfield broke his arm in a skateboarding accident
Dave Mustaine rejoined the band as a second guitarist
The band canceled the European leg due to visa issues

questions.scenario: It's 1972, and you're an aircraft engineer who has just seen test data proving the DC-10's rear cargo door latch can fail under pressure, much as it nearly did on an American Airlines flight over Windsor, Ontario. You draft a memo urging McDonnell Douglas management to act before more planes fly with the flaw.
questions.prompt: What does your memo recommend the manufacturer do?
questions.butterflyEffect: Management rejected the costly redesign and instead added a warning placard and a minor adjustment. Two years later, on 3 March 1974, the same door failure caused Flight 981 to break apart over Ermenonville, France, killing everyone aboard, and the disaster became a case study that pushed the FAA toward mandatory rather than voluntary safety fixes.

choices.text: A complete redesign of the cargo door's latching system
A warning placard instructing baggage handlers to double-check the door
No action, since the earlier incident had already been resolved
Grounding the entire DC-10 fleet for one week only

questions.scenario: You're an NTSB investigator in the days after 3 March 1991, examining wreckage of a United 737 that rolled over and dove into the ground on approach to Colorado Springs. Witnesses describe a sudden gust just before impact, but the flight recorders offer few clues.
questions.prompt: What ultimately explains the crash, confirmed only after two more 737s went down the same way?
questions.butterflyEffect: Investigators couldn't pin down a cause at the time, but after Eastwind Flight 517 and USAir Flight 427 suffered eerily similar upsets, the NTSB traced all three to a flaw in the Boeing 737's rudder power control unit that could jam and reverse. The finding forced a fleet-wide retrofit and changed how regulators treat recurring failures without a definitive black box answer.

choices.text: A rotor gust from mountain wave turbulence overwhelmed the aircraft
The captain suffered a sudden medical incapacitation
A jammed rudder power control unit forced the rudder to reverse
A bird strike disabled both engines simultaneously

questions.scenario: It's the evening of 3 March 2012, and you're a dispatcher on the Polish rail line near Szczekociny. Signals show two passenger trains converging onto the same stretch of track, and the window to stop them is closing fast.
questions.prompt: What should happen to prevent the collision?
questions.butterflyEffect: The warning was not acted on in time, and the two trains collided head-on, killing sixteen people and injuring dozens more. choices.text: Immediately halt both trains before they enter the shared track section
Let both continue, since the schedule allows a safe passing point
Reroute one train onto a freight-only siding without notifying the driver
Increase both trains' speed to clear the junction faster

questions.scenario: It's 3 March 1986, and you sit in the Australian Parliament as the Australia Act formally commences, severing the last legal threads tying Australian law to Westminster and the Privy Council.
questions.prompt: What immediate legal change follows from the Act's commencement?
questions.butterflyEffect: The Act ended appeals to the Privy Council and any British power to legislate for Australia, completing the country's legal independence from the United Kingdom. questions.butterflyEffect: Otho took his own life rather than prolong the civil war, becoming the second emperor to die in the chaotic Year of the Four Emperors. His death cleared the way for Vitellius, who would himself be overthrown and killed by Vespasian's forces before the year was out.

choices.text: Continue fighting with his remaining loyal troops

choices.text: Publicly swear an oath of innocence over the Gospels in St Peter's
Ask the Byzantine army to arrest his critics
Excommunicate every clergyman who doubts him
Abdicate and return quietly to Constantinople

questions.prompt: What do staff and bystanders do as the fire spreads through the building?
questions.butterflyEffect: Staff, firefighters and passersby formed chains to carry paintings and artworks out of the burning exchange before the dragon spire collapsed. questions.butterflyEffect: The aircraft lost control on landing and overran the runway, killing three people at the scene and a fourth later in hospital; the plane was destroyed. The crash prompted a review of Dornier 328 operations and runway safety margins at short coastal airports like Genoa.

questions.butterflyEffect: Civilians had painted the Russian word for "CHILDREN" in huge white letters on the ground outside the theatre, visible from the air. questions.butterflyEffect: The garrison held the castle, and its cannon fire kept Hertford's men from ever taking it, though much of the town and Holyrood were burned. questions.butterflyEffect: The killings prompted the U.S. military to launch the First Battle of Fallujah in April 2004, a major escalation that failed to fully pacify the city and was followed by an even larger Second Battle of Fallujah that November. The Anbar campaign that followed became one of the bloodiest and longest of the Iraq War.

choices.text: U.S. Marines launch the First Battle of Fallujah
American forces withdraw entirely from Anbar Province
A lasting ceasefire is negotiated with local insurgents
Security is quietly handed over to Iraqi police alone

questions.scenario: You are a recording engineer at the Victor studio in New York on 26 February 1917. A white New Orleans band wants to cut a rowdy, syncopated number full of barnyard imitations, and you must decide how to present it to the public.
questions.prompt: How should the record be marketed to capture what this new sound is?
questions.butterflyEffect: "Livery Stable Blues" became the first jazz record ever commercially released, and it was an immediate sensation, selling over a million copies. Its success launched the national jazz craze, though it also meant a white group got commercial credit ahead of the Black New Orleans musicians who had shaped the music for years.

choices.text: Label it plainly as a jazz record, a new type of music
Market it as a novelty ragtime comedy sketch
Bury it as a B-side and promote a waltz instead
Withhold release until a classically trained arranger cleans it up

choices.text: Publicly accept responsibility for the operation's mismanagement

Blame Congress for the Boland Amendment restrictions
Resign the presidency immediately

Withdraw all government officials from Tokyo until the rebels stand down

questions.butterflyEffect: The Philharmonic closed with the Korean folk song "Arirang," a piece beloved on both sides of the peninsula, moving many in the audience to tears. questions.prompt: How do you get back to France to claim the prize for reaching Timbuktu?
questions.butterflyEffect: Caillié joined a trans-Saharan caravan north to Fez, Morocco, then made his way to France, where the Paris Geographical Society awarded him its prize for reaching Timbuktu and returning alive. His account also punctured Europe's myth of a golden city, redirecting French colonial ambition toward the real resources of West Africa.

questions.prompt: What did the follow-up observations of GRB 970228 actually reveal?

questions.scenario: You stand in the Belfast shipyard on 26 February 1914 as White Star Line's newest liner, sister to the ill-fated Titanic, slides into the water for the first time. Company officials point out the changes made in direct response to the 1912 disaster.

questions.butterflyEffect: Britannic was fitted with a double hull along her engine rooms, raised watertight bulkheads, and davits capable of launching lifeboats even if the ship listed heavily. Yet when she struck a mine in the Aegean in 1916 while serving as a hospital ship, open portholes let water flood in far faster than designers anticipated, and she sank in under an hour, a lesson that further shaped maritime safety rules.

choices.text: Raised watertight bulkheads and lifeboat davits designed for a listing ship
A fully welded hull instead of riveted steel plates
Radar equipment to detect icebergs at night
A reduced passenger capacity to leave room for extra lifeboats only

questions.butterflyEffect: If Day, organised by Winnipeg's Victory Loan committee, dramatized a fictional Nazi occupation complete with a mock book-burning and staged arrests of officials. choices.text: To test the city's civil defense readiness
To sell Victory Bonds by showing citizens what Nazi occupation would look like
To recruit soldiers for overseas service
To protest wartime rationing policies

questions.butterflyEffect: Fort Henry surrendered after a brief bombardment, opening the Tennessee River to Union gunboats and forcing the Confederates to abandon nearby Fort Donelson soon after. The twin victories gave Grant his first major fame of the war and cracked open the Confederate defensive line across Kentucky and Tennessee.

choices.text: Fort Henry
Fort Sumter
Fort Donelson
Fort Pillow

questions.scenario: It is 25 February 1980 in Paramaribo. As Prime Minister Henck Arron, you learn that a group of sixteen non-commissioned officers, angry over pay and unionization, has seized the radio station and army barracks.
questions.prompt: What actually happened to Arron's government that day?
questions.butterflyEffect: The coup, led by Sergeant Major Dési Bouterse, toppled Arron and installed a military regime. choices.text: He negotiates a power-sharing deal that keeps him in office
He is overthrown and detained by the military coup plotters
He flees to the Netherlands before the coup begins
He orders the army to crush the mutiny within hours

questions.scenario: It is launch day, 25 February 1933, at Newport News shipyard. As a naval architect on the USS Ranger project, you must defend an unusual design choice: building America's first carrier planned from the keel up without a permanent island superstructure.
questions.prompt: Why was Ranger initially designed without an island?
questions.butterflyEffect: Naval planners believed a flat, unobstructed flight deck would maximize aircraft operations, so an island was omitted from the original design and only added after completion once its navigational drawbacks became clear. The lesson shaped every carrier built afterward, all of which received a proper island from the outset.

choices.text: To maximize flight-deck space for launching and landing aircraft
Because treaty tonnage limits forbade any superstructure
To reduce the ship's radar signature
Because the Navy had not yet decided if it would carry aircraft

questions.prompt: What did the Senate ultimately decide about seating Revels?
questions.butterflyEffect: The Senate voted 48–8 to seat Revels, making him the first African American to serve in Congress. His swearing-in was a landmark of Reconstruction, though it would be nearly a century before another Black senator was elected.

choices.text: It rejects him and orders a new Mississippi election
It votes to seat him despite the objections
It postpones the vote indefinitely without resolution
It seats him only after a constitutional amendment passes

questions.butterflyEffect: Marcos and his family were flown by U.S. military helicopters to Clark Air Base and then into exile in Hawaii, ending 20 years of rule. He is airlifted by the U.S. military into exile in Hawaii
He negotiates a ceasefire and remains as a figurehead president

questions.butterflyEffect: The member states agreed to dissolve the Pact's military structures, and the alliance was formally abolished later that year. questions.prompt: What followed in the years after James's coronation?
questions.butterflyEffect: James's Catholic faith and increasingly autocratic rule alienated Parliament and Protestant elites. questions.prompt: What did this landmark report call for as its central conclusion?
questions.butterflyEffect: The report concluded that smoking was a definite health hazard, particularly linked to lung cancer, setting off decades of regulation. questions.scenario: It is January 1923, and French and Belgian troops have just marched into Germany's industrial Ruhr Valley after Berlin fell behind on war reparations payments. questions.prompt: How did the German government respond to the occupation?
questions.butterflyEffect: Germany called for passive resistance, and workers went on strike rather than cooperate with the occupiers, causing the German economy to collapse into hyperinflation. questions.prompt: In whose honor was this new mission named?
questions.butterflyEffect: The mission was dedicated to Saint Clare of Assisi, founder of the Poor Clares, making it the first California mission honoring a woman. Saint Teresa of Ávila, the Spanish mystic and reformer

questions.scenario: It is the 1970s and you are a WHO epidemiologist tasked with eradicating smallpox worldwide, but vaccine supplies and staff are far too limited to inoculate every person on Earth.
questions.prompt: What strategy do you adopt to stop the disease with the resources available?
questions.butterflyEffect: Teams used surveillance-containment, or 'ring vaccination': tracking every outbreak and vaccinating everyone around it rather than whole populations. The approach succeeded, smallpox was declared eradicated in 1980, and the same ring-vaccination technique was later adapted to fight Ebola and polio outbreaks.

choices.text: Vaccinate entire national populations regardless of outbreaks
Track outbreaks and vaccinate everyone in contact with each case

Let natural infection build herd immunity over time

questions.prompt: What happens as the crowds surge toward Buckingham Palace?
questions.butterflyEffect: Winston Churchill and the royal family appeared together on the palace balcony to the roar of celebrating crowds, a scene that became the defining image of VE Day.
